clue.text: Chill! I'm the one ultimately working with a lot of cash (13 member)

indicators.note: letters that are working are set in motion and rearranged
ultimately points at the final letter of each of the three words before it
a lot of, not all of, means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: cash is money

explanation.surface: Someone is told to relax because they are the one sitting on a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix CHILL with M, E, E (the ends of I'm, the, one) for the first name; MONEY short of its last letter gives the surname. 13 is LORDS, so the definition means a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Baroness Mone sits in the House of Lords, so she is a peer, one of its members.

clue.text: See 1
The end is nigh

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a doom-monger's placard; the word means both a finish and nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a finish or conclusion; as an adjective it means near.

clue.text: One's old man going round demanding immediate attention

indicators.note: the two outer pieces going round something means they surround it

parts.note: an ex is a former partner, so ex- means old
a gent is a man
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is just 'is' joining the clue

explanation.surface: Someone's elderly husband is going about insisting on being seen to at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's old man' reads as a husband or father, but old and man are separate pieces wrapped around the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Exigent describes a situation or person that is urgent and pressing.

clue.text: Mock crazy American politician being detained

indicators.note: the American politician is being held inside, so those letters go within the other word

parts.note: a loon is a crazy person
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician

explanation.surface: Ridicule a mad US politician who has been locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To lampoon someone is to ridicule them in satire.

clue.text: Broad's day — Anderson finally overshadowed is puffing and blowing

indicators.note: a letter overshadowed by a word is covered by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: broad means wide; the 's is 'has', joining day on

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Anderson

explanation.surface: Stuart Broad has a big day as James Anderson, at last, is eclipsed and left breathless; both are England fast bowlers.
explanation.definitionFit: Being winded means being out of breath, gasping for air after effort.

clue.text: Naughty boy with Welshman getting stuck

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
Aled is a Welsh man's name, as in the singer Aled Jones

explanation.surface: A mischievous lad and a Welsh companion find themselves in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaled means pierced through by something sharp, run through by a spike.

clue.text: Suspect Padraig's stealing Henry's copying instruments

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means not to be trusted, so these letters are not in their true order

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance; stealing it means the name takes it into its letters

explanation.surface: A dubious Irishman, Padraig, is pilfering Henry's tracing gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Padraig's letters take in the H that 'stealing' adds, and 'Suspect' then rearranges the whole lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagraph is a drawing device for tracing or reproducing outlines, so these are drafting tools.

clue.text: You may show this in 'Top Gear'

definitions.text: You may show this in 'Top Gear'

parts.words: You may show this in 'Top Gear'
parts.note: Top Gear looks like the motoring TV show, but top gear here is smart clothing, and wearing it shows good taste in clothes

explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a British TV motoring programme; read instead as 'top gear', fine clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dress sense is good taste in choosing clothes, shown off by stylish outfits.

clue.text: Religious text that's evangelical not wholly uplifting

indicators.note: in a down clue uplifting means the letters are read from the bottom up
only part of the words is used, so the letters sit inside them

explanation.surface: A scripture whose evangelising tone is only partly inspiring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Avesta is the sacred scripture of Zoroastrianism.

clue.text: New moon — vagabond with Independent in element

parts.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter

indicators.note: in puts the Independent letter inside the vagabond

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant

explanation.surface: A new moon and a tramp in a newspaper's element story.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobium is a chemical element, a grey metal with atomic number 41.

clue.text: Struggle to accept idea for short cut taken by 1A/1A and 25 of 22's 24

definitions.text: short cut taken by 1A/1A and 25 of 22's 24

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
a plan is an idea or scheme

explanation.surface: Fighting to take on a scheme for a quick route used by the people in the PPE affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Michelle Mone and the landlord of Matt Hancock's local pub, both linked to pandemic PPE contracts.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'VIP lane' was the fast-track route for government pandemic supply contracts given to well-connected firms.

clue.text: Large deposit returned in class

indicators.note: in puts the reversed deposit inside the class

parts.note: a genus is a class in biology

indicators.note: returned means the word is read backwards

parts.note: ore is a mineral deposit

explanation.surface: A big refundable deposit is handed back during a class.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous can mean ample or plentiful, as in a generous helping.

clue.text: Way into the Spanish ground

indicators.note: into puts the way inside the Spanish article

parts.note: los is Spanish for 'the' (plural)
RD, road, is a way

explanation.surface: A route into Spanish territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London cricket ground; the word also means the House of Lords for the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord's is a famous sports venue, the home of cricket in London.

clue.text: While 24 varies, they do work on the surface

definitions.text: they do work on the surface

parts.note: as can mean while
24 is LOCAL, a pub, and PH is the map abbreviation for public house
alters means changes or varies

explanation.surface: While the pub changes, workers keep busy on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Asphalters lay tarmac, paving roads and paths with a bitumen top layer.

clue.text: Prats, you said! Bad spend wasted on this?

definitions.text: Prats, you said! Bad spend wasted on this?

indicators.note: wasted means ruined, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
said tells us 'you' is heard, and it sounds like the letter U

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: An outburst calling officials fools for squandering money on what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: public money was wasted on inferior protective equipment in the pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor-quality protective gear bought in the pandemic was a notorious waste of public spending.

clue.text: Getting as far as bridgehead before breaking through

indicators.note: bridgehead before means that letter is placed in front of the rest

parts.note: the head of bridge is its first letter
reaching means getting as far as

explanation.surface: Troops reach a bridgehead before smashing through enemy lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridgehead' looks like the military foothold, but it is the head, or first letter, of bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaching means making a gap in a wall or defence, forcing a way past it.

clue.text: Miners' leader with Conservative party?

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: Asks whether a union boss for coal miners joined a Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miners' leader' suggests a trade unionist; it is Doc, chief of Snow White's seven dwarfs, who worked in a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Disney film the dwarfs dig in a mine, and Doc is the one who leads them.

clue.text: See 15
What about having turn in shade?

indicators.note: in puts the turn inside the reversed word
about means the word turned around and read backwards

parts.note: eh is an exclamation meaning 'what?'
a U-turn is a turn, giving U

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about taking a turn in the shadows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hue is a colour or tint, a shade of something.

clue.text: Scientists in pieces over schmoe I experimented on

indicators.note: the pieces are placed over the other letters, covering them on both sides

parts.note: bits are pieces

indicators.note: letters experimented on are tried in new arrangements

explanation.surface: Researchers tear a hapless man apart after testing on him.
explanation.walkthrough: A schmoe is American slang for a fool or ordinary person.
explanation.definitionFit: Biochemists are scientists who study the chemistry of living things.

clue.text: Awkward layabout turned up — one he's looking after

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: a slob is a lazy layabout

indicators.note: he is looking after one, holding it in his care, so those letters go around it

parts.note: he, with the 's meaning 'is'
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A lazy person shows up, and he's caring for someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Bolshie is British slang for rebellious and uncooperative, from Bolshevik.

clue.text: Able to convert religious type

indicators.note: to convert something is to change it into a new form, here a new order of letters

explanation.surface: Someone who can convert people of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'convert' looks like the religious verb, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate is a layperson dedicated to a monastic life, a member of a religious community.

clue.text: See 27
Plant fuel — film planned on it

indicators.note: in a down clue the rearranged film is placed on the fuel, above it
planned means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A greenery-fuelled film project.
explanation.definitionFit: Milfoil is a plant, another name for yarrow or for a water weed.

clue.text: Confined though unlikely to put on weight

definitions.meaning: first meaning: restricted to a particular area

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as 'lo-cal', low in calories.
explanation.definitionFit: Local means limited to one area; lo-cal food is low in calories, so slimming.

clue.text: Comic coming back round with letter

indicators.note: round means the reversed word goes around the other
coming back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: droll means amusing, comic
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: A comedian returns with a piece of post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' looks like a written note, but it is one who lets property.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord is someone who lets property to tenants, so a 'let-ter'.

clue.text: England captain once seen with son in nightspot

indicators.note: in puts the son inside the captain's name

parts.note: Joe Root is a former England cricket captain

explanation.surface: A former England skipper is spotted with his boy at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nightspot' suggests a club; here it is where birds spend the night.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is a perch where birds settle to sleep at night.

clue.text: Can Chinese mate get signature?

parts.note: can and john are both slang for a toilet
the Han are the main ethnic group of China
cock is old Cockney slang for a mate, a pal

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Chinese friend can obtain an autograph.
explanation.walkthrough: John Hancock signed the US Declaration of Independence boldly, so his name is American slang for a signature.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a John Hancock means one's written name on a document.

clue.text: Describing height, 'petite' could be one

indicators.note: describing means drawing around, so the shuffled letters go around H
could be means the letters may become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A word describing someone's height, such as 'petite', is an example of the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: 'petite' is a word that describes height.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is a descriptive word or phrase applied to a person, like 'petite'.

clue.text: Knocked back very sweet old sherry

indicators.note: knocked back means turned around, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: so means very
a Rolo is a chocolate sweet

explanation.surface: Someone downed a very sweet old sherry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' suggests drinking; here it reverses the letters. Rolo is a British brand of chocolate sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Oloroso is a dark, full-bodied type of Spanish sherry.

clue.text: Sounded fed up talking about team

indicators.note: talking about signals a word heard aloud

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: Someone seemed glum when chatting about the team.
explanation.definitionFit: Sighed means let out a long breath, a sound of weariness or disappointment.

clue.text: Winter sport Bob may follow

parts.note: Bob looks like a man's name, but it is the bobsleigh; this head-first sled event shares its ice track and is run after it

explanation.walkthrough: Bob is short for bobsleigh, the event with which this sled race shares a track at the Winter Olympics.
explanation.definitionFit: Skeleton is a sledding race in which a rider lies face down on a small sled.
